summary.text: The second law of thermodynamics says heat flows spontaneously from hotter to colder regions, and that the entropy of an isolated system left alone cannot decrease.
It sets the direction of natural processes: a broken cup does not reassemble itself, though the first law alone would allow that.
It also limits engines, since not all heat can be converted into work in a cycle; Carnot showed in 1824 that conversion efficiency has an upper limit.

facts.label: Carnot's result
facts.value: In 1824, engine efficiency was shown to have an upper limit

facts.label: Clausius statement
facts.value: Heat never passes cold to warm without some other change

facts.label: Prominent statements
facts.value: Clausius in 1854, Kelvin in 1851, Carathéodory in 1909

facts.label: Arrow of time
facts.value: Rising entropy accounts for irreversible natural processes

facts.label: Microscopic basis
facts.value: Statistical mechanics explains it through probabilities of states

items.prompt: The pieces of a broken cup on the floor leap back together onto the table. Which statement is correct?

options.label: Energy conservation allows it, but the second law denies it
Energy conservation denies it, but the second law allows it
Both energy conservation and the second law allow it
Neither energy conservation nor the second law cares

items.explain: The first law permits the reverse process as well as the fall, but the second law denies the reversal.

items.prompt: A heat pump moves heat from cold outdoor air into a warm house. Does this break the second law?

options.label: Yes, because heat can never move from cold to warm
Yes, because pumps always create energy
No, because heat pumps are exempt from entropy
No, because the reversal still produces entropy in the surroundings

items.explain: A heat pump can reverse the flow, but the reversal process and the original one both produce entropy, raising the entropy of the surroundings.

items.prompt: An ice cube is dropped into a warm drink with nothing else going on. Which way does heat move?

options.label: From the ice into the drink
Back and forth with no net direction
From the drink into the ice
It stays put until the ice is stirred

items.explain: Heat flows spontaneously from a hotter body to a colder one whenever a path for conduction is available.

items.prompt: A sealed, insulated container is left alone to evolve on its own. Which way does its entropy move?

options.label: It can only fall
It stays exactly fixed
It rises and then falls back
It cannot fall and tends toward a maximum

items.explain: An isolated system left to spontaneous evolution cannot decrease its entropy and tends toward equilibrium, where entropy is highest.

items.prompt: An engineer proposes an engine that turns every bit of the heat it takes in each cycle into work. Why will it not exist?

options.label: Not all heat can be converted to work in a cycle
Engines can only run on electrical energy
Heat cannot be measured accurately enough
Work always destroys more energy than it uses

items.explain: One statement of the second law is that not all heat can be converted into work in a cyclic process, and Carnot showed efficiency has an upper limit.

items.prompt: A video of milk swirling into coffee looks wrong when played backward. What does thermodynamics offer as the reason?

options.label: The milk gains energy when it is un-mixed
Coffee cannot move without a spoon
Reversing would need the combined entropy to fall
Liquids can never change direction

items.explain: An increase in the combined entropy of system and surroundings accounts for the irreversibility of natural processes, the arrow of time.
